I found 9 explicit supersession records in project memory:

- `Explore primary MCP surface` (`CHANGELOG.md#2`): `codegraph_context` and `codegraph_trace` were removed in favor of `codegraph_explore`, replacing the earlier trace-dossier tool decision.
- `Marker-fenced agent instructions` (`CHANGELOG.md#3`): reintroduces installer-managed instruction content for subagent reach, superseding the earlier cleanup-only decision that stripped duplicate CodeGraph blocks.
- `Agent identity telemetry` (`CHANGELOG.md#3`): connected-agent telemetry is now collected, superseding the earlier proposed MCP `clientInfo` telemetry plumbing record.
- `Default-on value refs` (`docs/design/value-reference-edges.md#0`): provides the current shipped status and complete default-on language set, superseding the earlier partial default-on record from the playbook.
- `Whole-file family skeletonization` (`docs/design/adaptive-explore-sizing.md#1`): marks per-symbol family skeletonization as future work and says whole-file skeletonization cannot express it yet, so the earlier accepted per-symbol-focused decision should not remain current.
- `UI resolver extract rollout shipped`: the final Fix section supersedes the earlier node-only UI resolver migration with shipped extract rollout plus a narrower documented React Router handler gap.
- `Anonymous usage telemetry` (`CHANGELOG.md#3`): records the telemetry system as shipped and fully documented, replacing the earlier accepted design record whose description still said Worker deploy/DNS and release were pending.
- `ORM metaprogramming frontier` (`docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#4`): expands the existing ORM metaprogramming frontier with Spring Data JPA derived queries, so the prior narrower record is superseded rather than duplicated.
- `Subagent-visible CodeGraph guidance` (`CHANGELOG.md#3`): reverses the earlier `MCP guidance single source` requirement by showing that subagents need guidance in instruction files.

If you want, I can also list the earlier decisions each one replaced, as a before/after table.
